# Egami

> Egami is an MIT-licensed, fully managed 2D imaging library for .NET 10: it loads, edits, draws and saves images, with no
> native code and no third-party dependencies. The packages are Egami (rasters, pixel types, formats, operations, color
> management, metadata), Egami.Drawing (vector drawing on a canvas), Egami.Fonts (fonts, shaping and paragraph layout),
> Egami.Fonts.Substitutes (bundled metric-compatible fonts), Egami.Svg (SVG), Egami.Css (CSS) and Egami.Metafiles (WMF, EMF
> and EMF+).

Egami's own names: `Raster<TPixel>` and `Raster` hold images, pixel types such as `Rgba8` and `RgbaF32` say how pixels are
stored, `Raster.Load` and `Save` read and write files, `Raster.Probe` reads a file's size and format without decoding it,
`Apply` edits an image in place and `Derive` makes a new one, through a chain of operations, and `EgamiContext` holds the
settings, safety limits and registered formats a call uses.


## Docs

- [Getting started](https://inexin.github.io/Egami/v1/articles/getting-started.html): Egami loads, edits and saves images in .NET 10, in fully managed code.
- [Packages](https://inexin.github.io/Egami/v1/articles/packages.html): Egami is a family of packages.
- [Guides](https://inexin.github.io/Egami/v1/articles/guides/index.html): Each guide covers one area of Egami.

## Egami: basics

- [Benchmarks](https://inexin.github.io/Egami/v1/articles/benchmarks.html): How fast Egami is next to ImageSharp, SkiaSharp and Magick.NET on the same tasks and inputs.
- [Diagnostics](https://inexin.github.io/Egami/v1/articles/diagnostics.html): Egami can tell an app what it recovered from, what it lost on purpose and what it decided on the caller's behalf, through one optional handler on `EgamiContext`.
- [Memory and threading](https://inexin.github.io/Egami/v1/articles/guides/memory-and-threading.html): A raster remembers the context it was loaded or created with, and its operations use it.
- [Metadata](https://inexin.github.io/Egami/v1/articles/guides/metadata.html): `raster.Metadata` holds what a file says beside its pixels.
- [Performance](https://inexin.github.io/Egami/v1/articles/performance.html): Tips that keep loading, editing and saving fast, how to run the benchmarks, and Egami's numbers.
- [Pixel types](https://inexin.github.io/Egami/v1/articles/guides/pixel-types.html): A raster stores one pixel type, chosen when you load or create it.
- [Security](https://inexin.github.io/Egami/v1/articles/guides/security.html): Egami is built to open files from people you do not trust.

## Formats

- [Overview](https://inexin.github.io/Egami/v1/articles/formats/index.html): Egami reads and writes PNG, APNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, BMP, TGA, QOI and the Netpbm formats (PBM, PGM, PPM, PAM and the PFM float map), TIFF, Radiance .hdr, OpenEXR, JPEG XL, AVIF, and Windows icons and …
- [ANI](https://inexin.github.io/Egami/v1/articles/formats/ani.html): Egami reads and writes Windows animated cursors (.ani), written from Microsoft's description of the RIFF `ACON` form.
- [AVIF](https://inexin.github.io/Egami/v1/articles/formats/avif.html): Egami reads and writes AVIF still images, written from the AV1 and HEIF specifications with no native code.
- [AV1 video frames](https://inexin.github.io/Egami/v1/articles/formats/av1.html): `Av1StreamDecoder` decodes AV1 video a temporal unit at a time and `Av1StreamEncoder` encodes it; both work on frames, and Egami.Video uses them for its containers.
- [BMP](https://inexin.github.io/Egami/v1/articles/formats/bmp.html): Egami reads Windows bitmaps with core, info, V2 to V5 and OS/2 2.x headers at 1 to 32 bits, RLE4, RLE8 and RLE24, OS/2 Huffman 1D, bit fields, embedded PNG and JPEG and V5 ICC profiles.
- [Camera RAW](https://inexin.github.io/Egami/v1/articles/formats/raw.html): Camera RAW files hold the sensor data a camera recorded, before any processing.
- [CCITT fax](https://inexin.github.io/Egami/v1/articles/formats/ccitt.html): Egami decodes raw CCITT fax data.
- [DDS](https://inexin.github.io/Egami/v1/articles/formats/dds.html): DDS (DirectDraw Surface, .dds) is the texture container of Direct3D and most game engines.
- [Extended formats](https://inexin.github.io/Egami/v1/articles/formats/extended.html): Egami.Formats.Extended reads and writes image formats that most apps never meet but some still need.
- [Farbfeld](https://inexin.github.io/Egami/v1/articles/formats/farbfeld.html): Farbfeld is suckless.org's lossless format.
- [GIF](https://inexin.github.io/Egami/v1/articles/formats/gif.html): Egami reads GIF 87a and 89a files, with every disposal method, interlaced images, transparency, the loop count, comments, XMP and ICC profiles, and writes GIF 89a.
- [HEIC](https://inexin.github.io/Egami/v1/articles/formats/heic.html): HEIC is the format iPhones and most Android phones save photos in.
- [ICNS](https://inexin.github.io/Egami/v1/articles/formats/icns.html): Egami reads and writes Apple icon families (.icns), written from Apple's description of the format.
- [ICO and CUR](https://inexin.github.io/Egami/v1/articles/formats/ico.html): Egami reads and writes Windows icons (.ico) and cursors (.cur), written from Microsoft's documentation of the icon directory.
- [ISO BMFF boxes](https://inexin.github.io/Egami/v1/articles/formats/iso-boxes.html): MP4, QuickTime, HEIF, HEIC and AVIF files are made of boxes (ISO/IEC 14496-12).
- [JBIG2](https://inexin.github.io/Egami/v1/articles/formats/jbig2.html): Egami reads JBIG2 (ITU-T T.88 | ISO/IEC 14492), the bi-level format of scanned documents and of the JBIG2Decode images in PDF, written from the 2018 edition of T.88 and the PDF specification.
- [JPEG](https://inexin.github.io/Egami/v1/articles/formats/jpeg.html): JPEG files load like any other.
- [JPEG 2000](https://inexin.github.io/Egami/v1/articles/formats/jpeg2000.html): Egami reads JPEG 2000 (ITU-T T.800 | ISO/IEC 15444-1, all of Part 1), written from the 2019 edition of T.800, T.801's JPX boxes and the PDF specification's JPXDecode filter.
- [JPEG XL](https://inexin.github.io/Egami/v1/articles/formats/jxl.html): Egami reads and writes JPEG XL (ISO/IEC 18181), written from the specification with no native code.
- [Netpbm](https://inexin.github.io/Egami/v1/articles/formats/pnm.html): Egami reads and writes the Netpbm formats.
- [OpenEXR](https://inexin.github.io/Egami/v1/articles/formats/openexr.html): `ExrFormat` reads scanline and tiled files, single and multi-part (`ExrPartKind`), with every compression of OpenEXR 3 (`ExrCompression`.
- [PCX](https://inexin.github.io/Egami/v1/articles/formats/pcx.html): PCX is ZSoft's PC Paintbrush format.
- [PNG and APNG](https://inexin.github.io/Egami/v1/articles/formats/png.html): Egami reads and writes PNG and its animated form, APNG.
- [PSD and PSB](https://inexin.github.io/Egami/v1/articles/formats/psd.html): Egami reads Adobe Photoshop documents (.psd) and large documents (.psb), written from Adobe's Photoshop File Format Specification.
- [QOI](https://inexin.github.io/Egami/v1/articles/formats/qoi.html): Egami reads and writes the whole Quite OK Image format, with 3 or 4 channels and both colorspaces.
- [Radiance](https://inexin.github.io/Egami/v1/articles/formats/radiance.html): Radiance pictures hold three 8-bit mantissas and a shared exponent per pixel (RGBE), or CIE X, Y and Z the same way (XYZE).
- [SGI](https://inexin.github.io/Egami/v1/articles/formats/sgi.html): SGI is Silicon Graphics' image format (.rgb, .rgba, .bw, .sgi).
- [Sun raster](https://inexin.github.io/Egami/v1/articles/formats/sun-raster.html): Sun raster is the rasterfile format of SunOS.
- [TGA](https://inexin.github.io/Egami/v1/articles/formats/tga.html): Egami reads Truevision TGA files.
- [TIFF](https://inexin.github.io/Egami/v1/articles/formats/tiff.html): Egami reads and writes TIFF and BigTIFF, written from the TIFF 6.0 specification, Adobe's technical notes and supplements and the BigTIFF design note, starting from the reader in Lars's ClassicMac.
- [VP8 video frames](https://inexin.github.io/Egami/v1/articles/formats/vp8.html): `Vp8StreamDecoder` decodes VP8 video frame by frame and `Vp8StreamEncoder` encodes it; both work on frames, and Egami.Video uses them for WebM, Matroska and IVF files.
- [WBMP](https://inexin.github.io/Egami/v1/articles/formats/wbmp.html): WBMP is the Wireless Application Protocol's one-bit bitmap.
- [WebP](https://inexin.github.io/Egami/v1/articles/formats/webp.html): Egami reads and writes WebP.
- [XBM](https://inexin.github.io/Egami/v1/articles/formats/xbm.html): XBM is the X Window System's one-bit bitmap, written as C source.
- [XPM](https://inexin.github.io/Egami/v1/articles/formats/xpm.html): XPM, the X PixMap format, is C source holding an array of strings.
- [Your own format](https://inexin.github.io/Egami/v1/articles/formats/custom.html): Egami's formats are plug-ins like any other.

## Egami: editing images

- [Color](https://inexin.github.io/Egami/v1/articles/guides/color.html): Color operations follow the W3C Filter Effects definitions, so they match what a browser's CSS `filter` does.
- [Compositing](https://inexin.github.io/Egami/v1/articles/guides/compositing.html): `DrawImage` draws one raster onto another with source-over blending.
- [Edges and morphology](https://inexin.github.io/Egami/v1/articles/guides/edges-and-morphology.html): Edge operators measure how fast the image changes at each pixel; Canny's detector turns that into thin edge lines; and morphology grows, shrinks and cleans up shapes by taking the maximum or minimum …
- [Effects and shadows](https://inexin.github.io/Egami/v1/articles/guides/effects.html): The editor's effects menu.
- [Filters](https://inexin.github.io/Egami/v1/articles/guides/filters.html): `Blur(sigma)` computes the exact Gaussian, so its cost grows with sigma.
- [Keying and arithmetic](https://inexin.github.io/Egami/v1/articles/guides/keying-and-arithmetic.html): Operations that ImageMagick users expect.
- [Lighting and relief](https://inexin.github.io/Egami/v1/articles/guides/lighting-and-relief.html): Three steps treat an image as a height field and light it.
- [Regions, masks and channels](https://inexin.github.io/Egami/v1/articles/guides/regions-and-masks.html): Any chain that keeps the image's size can run on part of the image.
- [Resizing and geometry](https://inexin.github.io/Egami/v1/articles/guides/resizing-and-geometry.html): Every operation is a step in a chain you record in a lambda.
- [Tone and color](https://inexin.github.io/Egami/v1/articles/guides/tone-and-color.html): Egami has the tone and color tools photo editors have.

## Egami: color and HDR

- [Color management](https://inexin.github.io/Egami/v1/articles/guides/color-management.html): Egami reads color information from every file and keeps it, but changes no pixel unless you ask.
- [HDR images](https://inexin.github.io/Egami/v1/articles/guides/hdr.html): HDR images hold light brighter than SDR white.
- [Planar YUV](https://inexin.github.io/Egami/v1/articles/guides/planar-yuv.html): A `YuvRaster` holds a picture as separate luma (Y) and chroma (U, V) planes, plus an optional alpha plane.

## Egami: analysis, palettes and animation

- [Animation](https://inexin.github.io/Egami/v1/articles/guides/animation.html): A raster holds one or more frames, all the size of the raster and the same pixel type.
- [Comparing and measuring](https://inexin.github.io/Egami/v1/articles/guides/analysis.html): Calls that look at images rather than change them.
- [Palettes and dithering](https://inexin.github.io/Egami/v1/articles/guides/palettes.html): The palette machinery behind the GIF, palette PNG, BMP and TGA writers, opened up.
- [Text recognition (OCR)](https://inexin.github.io/Egami/v1/articles/guides/ocr.html): Egami does not recognize text itself.

## Egami: extending

- [Custom operations and formats](https://inexin.github.io/Egami/v1/articles/guides/extending.html): Everything here uses only Egami's public API; Egami's own test suite has an outside project that does each of these things.

## Egami.Drawing

- [Drawing](https://inexin.github.io/Egami/v1/articles/guides/drawing.html): Egami.Drawing is a separate package that draws antialiased paths, shapes, strokes, clips and images on a `Canvas`.
- [Drawing files (.egdr)](https://inexin.github.io/Egami/v1/articles/guides/egdr-format.html): An Egami drawing file holds a recorded `Picture`.

## Egami.Fonts

- [Fonts and text](https://inexin.github.io/Egami/v1/articles/guides/text.html): Egami.Fonts is a separate package that reads TrueType, OpenType, WOFF, WOFF2 and variable fonts in managed code.
- [Paragraph layout](https://inexin.github.io/Egami/v1/articles/guides/paragraph-layout.html): Egami.Fonts lays out paragraphs in the `Egami.Fonts.Layout` namespace.
- [Unicode text and shaping](https://inexin.github.io/Egami/v1/articles/guides/unicode-text.html): Egami.Fonts carries its own Unicode 17.0 data and the Unicode algorithms text shaping builds on.
- [Matching System.Drawing](https://inexin.github.io/Egami/v1/articles/guides/system-drawing-text.html): Egami can draw the way System.Drawing does on Windows.

## Egami.Svg and Egami.Css

- [CSS](https://inexin.github.io/Egami/v1/articles/guides/css.html): Egami.Css parses and applies CSS in managed code, with no dependencies.
- [SVG](https://inexin.github.io/Egami/v1/articles/guides/svg.html): Egami.Svg reads SVG 1.1 and SVG 2 files into an editable element tree, saves them back, and draws them through Egami.Drawing's canvas, so the same document renders to a raster, to a PDF page or back …

## Egami.Metafiles

- [Windows metafiles](https://inexin.github.io/Egami/v1/articles/guides/metafiles.html): Egami.Metafiles plays Windows metafiles, the vector pictures Office and Windows programs exchange.

## Egami.Formats.Extended

- [Developing camera RAW](https://inexin.github.io/Egami/v1/articles/guides/camera-raw.html): A camera RAW file holds what the sensor recorded.
- [Textures](https://inexin.github.io/Egami/v1/articles/guides/textures.html): Game engines and 3D tools keep their textures in DDS files.

## Egami.SystemDrawing

- [Migrating from System.Drawing to Egami](https://inexin.github.io/Egami/v1/articles/guides/system-drawing-migration.html): Egami.SystemDrawing runs System.Drawing code unchanged; this guide moves that code to Egami's own API one piece at a time, with the four escape hatches that join the two.
- [System.Drawing drop-in](https://inexin.github.io/Egami/v1/articles/guides/system-drawing.html): Egami.SystemDrawing gives code written for System.Drawing.Common its API on every OS, in managed code.

## Egami.Video

- [Video](https://inexin.github.io/Egami/v1/articles/guides/video.html): Egami.Video reads and writes video with Egami rasters as frames, so resizing, color and drawing from Egami work on video with no copying.
- [Streaming MP4](https://inexin.github.io/Egami/v1/articles/guides/streaming-mp4.html): Flat MP4 needs its index (moov) before or after all of the media, so a writer must either seek back or hold the media somewhere until the end.
- [Encoding video](https://inexin.github.io/Egami/v1/articles/guides/video-encoding.html): Egami.Video encodes VP8 and VP9 into WebM, Matroska and IVF (VP9 into MP4 too), with alpha in WebM and Matroska, and AV1 into WebM, Matroska, MP4, IVF, raw OBU and Annex B files.
- [Video editing](https://inexin.github.io/Egami/v1/articles/guides/video-editing.html): Egami.Video's editing library, in `Egami.Video.Editing`, joins clips with transitions, draws clips over clips, keys out green screens, lays clips side by side and runs Egami operations on the result …
- [Lossless archiving with FFV1](https://inexin.github.io/Egami/v1/articles/guides/lossless-archiving.html): FFV1 (RFC 9043) is the lossless video codec memory institutions archive with.
- [H.264](https://inexin.github.io/Egami/v1/articles/guides/h264.html): Egami.Video.H264 decodes H.264 (AVC), the codec of most MP4 and MOV files from phones, cameras and the web.
- [HEVC](https://inexin.github.io/Egami/v1/articles/guides/hevc.html): Egami.Video.Hevc decodes HEVC (H.265), the codec of iPhone and Android video, GoPro footage, 4K streaming and HDR10.
- [Audio](https://inexin.github.io/Egami/v1/articles/guides/audio.html): Egami.Video decodes and encodes audio with the same send and receive loop as video.
- [Audio filters](https://inexin.github.io/Egami/v1/articles/guides/audio-filters.html): Egami.Video's audio filters change level, time, tone and placement of decoded audio as it streams.
- [Encoding Opus](https://inexin.github.io/Egami/v1/articles/guides/opus-encoding.html): Opus (RFC 6716) is the audio codec of WebM and of .opus files, and the best general-purpose lossy codec for both speech and music.
- [Subtitles](https://inexin.github.io/Egami/v1/articles/guides/subtitles.html): Egami.Video reads and writes text subtitle files in the `Egami.Video.Subtitles` namespace.

## Egami.Video.Cli

- [The egami-video command](https://inexin.github.io/Egami/v1/articles/video-cli/index.html): `egami-video` inspects, remuxes, cuts, joins and converts video and audio files from a shell or a build script, with no C# to write.
- [Command reference](https://inexin.github.io/Egami/v1/articles/video-cli/commands.html): Every egami-video command with its arguments and options, as `egami-video <command> --help` prints them.
- [ffmpeg command lines](https://inexin.github.io/Egami/v1/articles/video-cli/ffmpeg.html): `egami-video ffmpeg` and `egami-video ffprobe` take the command lines people already know, find in answers online or have in scripts, and run them with egami-video's own commands.
- [egami-video for AI assistants](https://inexin.github.io/Egami/v1/articles/video-cli/assistants.html): `egami-video mcp` serves egami-video's commands as tools to an AI assistant (Claude, GitHub Copilot, Cursor) over the Model Context Protocol, on standard input and output.

## Egami.Barcodes

- [Barcodes](https://inexin.github.io/Egami/v1/articles/guides/barcodes.html): Egami.Barcodes writes and reads barcodes.
- [Reading barcodes](https://inexin.github.io/Egami/v1/articles/guides/barcode-reading.html): Egami.Barcodes reads every symbology it writes.

## Egami.Cli

- [The egami command](https://inexin.github.io/Egami/v1/articles/cli/index.html): `egami` converts, inspects, resizes and edits images from a shell or a build script, with no C# to write.
- [Command reference](https://inexin.github.io/Egami/v1/articles/cli/commands.html): Every egami command with its arguments and options, as `egami <command> --help` prints them.
- [Steps for run](https://inexin.github.io/Egami/v1/articles/cli/steps.html): The steps `egami run` chains and workflow files list.
- [egami for AI assistants](https://inexin.github.io/Egami/v1/articles/cli/assistants.html): `egami mcp` serves egami's commands to an AI assistant, such as Claude, GitHub Copilot or Cursor, over the Model Context Protocol.
